notes:
The whole list is on n140.jpg (p. 123, 'IRISH COAST'). Pages n136–n139 (pp. 119–122) hold only the introductory text, signed Richard M. Barrington and Alexander G. More. I didn't open n141–n143 because the list ends on n140 with its key printed below it.

Column order as printed: No., station and county, Schedules Filled, Spring, Autumn, Miles from Shore, Names of Observers. This differs from the other reader's description: 'Schedules Filled' comes before Spring and Autumn, not after. The list has no column for the light's character.

Key printed under the table: 'o=No reply.  x=Schedule returned partly or wholly filled.  Spring, replies received, 24.  Autumn, replies received, 22.' My count of the x marks agrees: 24 spring and 22 autumn. Stations with no reply also have 'o' in the Schedules Filled column, which looks like the letter o rather than a zero. I've kept it as 'o'.

Numbering: 5.* (Coningbeg Lt.-ship) and 8.* (Arklow North Lt.-ship) are starred insertions after 5 and 8. Numbers 9, 18 and 35 don't appear at all. 8.* clearly reads 8 and not 9, in line with 5.*. The star seems to mark light-ships added to the map, but Barrels Rock (6) and Kish Bank (10), also light-ships, are not starred.

'do.' means Wexford for Barrels Rock and Tuskar Rock, and Wicklow for Arklow North. Tuskar Rock is printed without 'Lt.-ship'. For 'Old Head, Kinsale, Cork' I split the entry as name 'Old Head' and place 'Kinsale, Cork', meaning the Old Head of Kinsale.

'No reply.' is printed in italics in the observers column. I've written it as _No reply._ in printed and put it in other, not keepers. A '–' in Miles from Shore is printed as such (no distance given). Dursey Island has '½'.

Two-line observer entries (Coningbeg, Tuskar, Arklow Sth., Rockabill) have a brace '{' in front of the names. It groups the names, not the station, so I haven't put it in marks. I split joint entries into individual people, keeping each name exactly as printed: 'Patrick Cullen and Wm. Clydesdale'; 'Rd. Hamilton, Peter Page, & E. M‘Kenna' (very tightly spaced in print, 'Hamilton,Peter Page,&E.'); 'Patrick Clancy and Alfred B. Wall'; 'Jos. Hammond and Henry Kelly'. 'Wm.Higginbotham.' is also tightly set; I've written it with a normal space.

In printed I've shortened the dot leaders to '...' and left out the end-of-row full stop from the keeper names. M‘Carron, M‘Cabe and M‘Kenna use a turned comma (‘), and O’Birne and O’Donnell use an apostrophe.

The list has 'Michael Cunniam.' followed by a faint speck, probably a printing mark (the OCR's 'Cunniam.-'). The name could be a misprint for Cunningham, but I've copied it as printed.

Spellings copied as printed: 'Howth Baily' (Baily lighthouse), 'Innishtrahull', 'Arranmore', 'Arran Island' (Aran), 'Valentia'. 'John A. Murray' is named at both Rathlin (15) and Broadhaven (24). That's either the same man listed twice or two keepers with the same name.

The OCR garbles several stations completely: Fastnet, Rathlin, Blackrock, Skelligs, and the names of Maidens and Barrels Rock. Its separate columns can't be lined up with the rows reliably, so every entry here was read from the image.
